subject: health
unitTitle: Mental and Emotional Health: Stress, Coping, and Help-Seeking
title: Guided practice: building a personal regulation routine
essentialQuestion: How do I manage stress in a way that still works on a bad week, and how do I ask for help early?
materials: a guardian-approved list of local and national help resources
keyPoints: A regulation routine pairs an early signal with a brief action, a practical next step, and a support option; it should be simple enough to use under stress.
Match the response to the level of need: use a practical coping step for ordinary strain, add trusted support when functioning is disrupted, and use urgent help for immediate danger.
For building a personal regulation routine, a strong response distinguishes fact from assumption, uses a fictional or public case, and includes a safe next step or appropriate source of support.
privacySafeScenario: Build a two-tier support plan: strategies the learner can run alone, and the named point at which they contact a trusted adult or professional. The plan may be written entirely with general categories rather than personal detail.
studentTask: Complete a fictional support-plan card for building a personal regulation routine: identify one observable signal, choose one immediate coping or communication step, name a routine support route and an urgent route, and explain why the plan does not make a peer responsible for care.
knowledgeCheck: In two or three sentences, explain the most important distinction in building a personal regulation routine; use one lesson fact and name the evidence, safety check, or support route that makes the explanation dependable.
completionCriteria: The response completes every named part of the building a personal regulation routine task using the supplied fictional or public case.
The response uses at least two accurate details from the lesson instruction and distinguishes evidence from assumption.
The response gives a safe, feasible next step or support route and does not depend on private disclosure, body comparison, or recorded media proof.
adaptationChoices: Coping strategies may be movement-based, still, sensory, verbal, written, or silent; every learner selects strategies their body and setting actually allow. Responses may be selected from options rather than composed.
extensionChallenge: Apply building a personal regulation routine under a new constraint, compare two approaches, or explain the idea to someone else with an original fictional example, without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.

trustedAdultNote: This course teaches health information and does not diagnose; direct urgent safety or health concerns to a trusted adult or qualified professional.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of building a personal regulation routine in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or private disclosure is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.

contentProvenance.objective: Explain building a personal regulation routine accurately using current, reliable health information rather than assumption or anecdote.
